title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow
plain: The computer sees a problem with how much exhaust gas is being fed back into the engine by the EGR system. Too much or too little flow can both set this code.
symptoms: Rough idle or stalling if the EGR is stuck open
Pinging or knocking when accelerating if the EGR is not flowing

causes.name: Carbon buildup clogging the EGR valve or passages
Bad EGR pressure or position sensor
Cracked or disconnected vacuum hose to the EGR valve
Faulty EGR control solenoid or wiring

checks: Look for other EGR codes that narrow down the problem
Inspect vacuum hoses and wiring at the EGR valve
Check whether the EGR valve opens and closes when commanded with a scan tool
fix: Usually cleaning carbon from the EGR valve and passages or replacing the EGR valve.
drive: Usually you can keep driving and book a repair. If the engine stalls at stops or idles very rough, the valve may be stuck open; limit driving, since stalling in traffic is risky. If you hear pinging under load, avoid hard acceleration to protect the engine.
test_first: Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and watch engine response, check the passages for carbon, and test the EGR sensor and vacuum supply before replacing the valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient Detected
plain: The EGR system is supposed to send a small amount of exhaust back into the engine to keep combustion cooler, and the computer sees too little of it getting through.
symptoms: Pinging or spark knock under acceleration or uphill
Usually no other change in how the car drives

causes.name: Faulty EGR pressure (DPFE) or position sensor
Leaking or disconnected vacuum line or bad EGR vacuum solenoid
Cracked sensor hoses on the DPFE sensor

checks: Inspect the EGR valve and intake passages for heavy carbon
Check vacuum hoses and DPFE sensor hoses for cracks
Watch EGR position or pressure readings on a scan tool while the valve is commanded open
fix: Most often cleaning clogged EGR passages or replacing the EGR valve or its pressure sensor.
examples: Well known on older Ford models with a DPFE sensor
Common on older Honda engines with clogged intake EGR ports
drive: Usually you can keep driving and schedule a repair. If you hear pinging when accelerating or climbing hills, avoid hard acceleration and heavy towing, since ongoing knock can harm the engine. It may cause a failed emissions test.
test_first: Check the EGR passages and ports for carbon, check vacuum lines and the DPFE sensor hoses, and confirm the valve opens when commanded before replacing the valve or sensor.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive Detected
plain: Too much exhaust gas is being fed back into the engine, often because the EGR valve is stuck open. That can make the engine idle rough or stall.
symptoms: Rough idle or stalling, especially when stopping

causes.name: EGR valve stuck open from carbon
Faulty EGR pressure (DPFE) or position sensor
Faulty EGR control solenoid stuck on
Wrong vacuum hose routing to the EGR valve
Wiring fault to the EGR solenoid

checks: Check if the idle smooths out with the EGR valve unplugged or blocked off
Inspect the EGR valve for carbon holding it open
Compare EGR sensor readings at idle with the valve closed
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the EGR valve, or replacing a faulty EGR sensor or solenoid.
drive: Get it checked soon. An EGR valve stuck open can make the engine stall when you stop, which is risky in traffic. If it stalls or idles very rough, keep trips short and go straight to a shop. If it runs normally, drive gently and book a repair.
test_first: Check whether the EGR valve is stuck open with carbon, verify vacuum hose routing and solenoid operation, and test the DPFE or position sensor before replacing the valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Control Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit that controls the EGR valve or its control solenoid, so it cannot operate the valve properly.

causes.name: Failed EGR valve or EGR control solenoid coil
Damaged or corroded connector at the EGR valve
Blown fuse feeding the EGR circuit

checks: Inspect the EGR connector for corrosion and loose pins
Measure the EGR solenoid resistance against spec
Check for power and ground at the connector with the key on
fix: Most often a new EGR valve or EGR control solenoid; sometimes a wiring or connector repair.
drive: Usually you can keep driving and book a repair soon. Avoid hard acceleration if you hear pinging. If the engine idles rough or stalls, get it checked sooner, since stalling in traffic is risky.
test_first: Check the fuse, connector and wiring to the EGR valve or solenoid, measure the coil's resistance, and confirm the computer's command signal before replacing parts.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The EGR valve is not moving to the position the computer asks for, usually because carbon is making it stick or the valve is wearing out.
symptoms: Rough idle or stalling if the valve sticks open
Pinging under acceleration if it sticks closed

causes.name: Carbon buildup making the EGR valve stick
Faulty EGR position sensor in the valve
Wiring or connector problem at the valve
Vacuum supply problem on vacuum-operated valves

checks: Command the EGR open and closed with a scan tool and watch actual position
Remove and inspect the valve for carbon
Check the connector and wiring for damage
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the EGR valve.
drive: Usually you can keep driving and book a repair. If the engine stalls at stops or idles very rough, the valve may be sticking open; limit driving, since stalling in traffic is risky. If you hear pinging under load, avoid hard acceleration.
test_first: Compare actual and commanded EGR position on a scan tool, check for carbon sticking the valve and the vacuum supply, and inspect the connector before replacing the valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low
plain: The sensor that tells the computer how much the EGR valve is open, or how much exhaust is flowing, is sending a signal that is lower than possible.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Failed EGR position or pressure (DPFE) sensor
Failed EGR valve with built-in sensor

checks: Read the sensor voltage with key on and engine off
Check the 5 volt reference and ground at the sensor
Inspect wiring for chafing against the engine or exhaust
fix: Usually replacing the EGR sensor, or the EGR valve if the sensor is built in.

cost.job: Replace EGR position or pressure sensor

drive: Usually you can keep driving and book a repair; the car often drives normally. If you hear pinging under load, avoid hard acceleration and get it checked sooner.
test_first: Check the sensor's reference voltage, ground and signal at the connector for a short to ground, and test the sensor before replacing the EGR valve or sensor.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High
plain: The EGR position or pressure sensor is sending a signal that is higher than it should ever be, which usually points to a wiring or sensor problem.

causes.name: Failed EGR position or pressure sensor
Failed EGR valve with built-in sensor

checks: Check sensor voltage and ground at the connector
Inspect the connector for water or corrosion
fix: Usually replacing the EGR sensor or the EGR valve assembly, or repairing wiring.

cost.job: Replace EGR position or pressure sensor

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit Low
plain: On engines with a second EGR sensor, that sensor is reading lower than possible, usually from a wiring short or a failed sensor.
checks: Check the sensor signal and reference voltage at the connector
Inspect wiring for chafing
fix: Replace the faulty sensor or repair the wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit High
plain: The second EGR sensor is reading higher than possible, which usually means an open wire or a bad sensor.
checks: Check the sensor ground and signal at the connector
Look for broken or corroded wiring
fix: Replace the faulty sensor or repair the wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: The computer sees a general electrical fault in the EGR sensor "A" circuit, such as a signal that drops out or makes no sense.

causes.name: Failed EGR position or pressure sensor
Failed EGR valve with built-in sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Watch the sensor reading on a scan tool for dropouts while wiggling the harness
fix: Usually a new EGR sensor or EGR valve, or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: The computer sees an electrical problem with the sensor that measures the temperature of the recirculated exhaust gas. This sensor is mostly found on diesels and some newer gas engines.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Usually a new EGR temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The EGR temperature sensor is giving readings that do not make sense for how the engine is running, such as staying the same when it should change.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions

causes.name: Failed or sluggish EGR temperature sensor
Clogged EGR cooler or passages changing the gas temperature

checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Usually a new EGR temperature sensor; check the EGR cooler and valve too.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "A" Circuit Low
plain: The EGR temperature sensor signal is lower than it should ever be, usually from a short in the wiring or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the shorted wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "A" Circuit High
plain: The EGR temperature sensor signal is higher than it should ever be, which often means an open wire or unplugged sensor.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the broken wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The EGR temperature sensor signal is jumping around or cutting in and out.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions

causes.name: Wiring rubbing through near the exhaust

checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace the sensor.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "A"/"B" Correlation
plain: On engines with two EGR temperature sensors, their readings do not agree with each other the way the computer expects.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions

causes.name: Wiring problem on one of the sensors

checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Compare both sensor readings, then replace the faulty sensor or fix the EGR cooler.

title: Secondary Air Injection System
plain: Many engines pump fresh air into the exhaust right after a cold start to help the catalytic converter warm up faster. The computer found a problem with that air injection system.
symptoms: Loud whine or roar from the air pump after a cold start, or no pump noise at all
Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Stuck or leaking air check (combination) valve
Blown fuse or bad air pump relay
Cracked air hoses or clogged air passages
Wiring problem to the pump or valve

checks: Listen for the air pump running for a minute or so after a cold start
Check the air pump fuse and relay
Inspect the check valve and hoses for moisture, carbon and cracks
fix: Often a new air pump and check valve; sometimes just a relay, fuse or hose.
examples: Air pumps that take in water and seize are a frequent cause
drive: Usually you can keep driving; this system mainly cuts emissions for the first minute or so after a cold start. Get it repaired before an emissions test. If you notice a burning smell near the pump or the fuse keeps blowing, get it checked sooner.
test_first: Check the fuse and relay, listen for the pump on a cold start, test the check valve for sticking or leaks, and check hoses and passages before replacing the pump.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow Detected
plain: The system that blows fresh air into the exhaust during cold starts is not moving the amount of air the computer expects.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Air pump may sound unusually loud or quiet on cold start

causes.name: Weak or failed secondary air pump
Faulty upstream oxygen sensor reading the wrong result

checks: Run the air pump with a scan tool and watch upstream O2 sensor readings go lean
Check hoses and the check valve for leaks or blockage
Check the pump fuse and relay
fix: Usually replacing the air pump or the switching/check valve, or clearing blocked passages.
drive: Usually you can keep driving; this system mainly cuts emissions for the first minute or so after a cold start. Get it repaired before an emissions test. If you notice a burning smell near the pump or the fuse keeps blowing, get it checked sooner.
test_first: Check pump output on a cold start, test the check and switching valves, look for blocked passages and leaking hoses, and confirm the oxygen sensor responds correctly before replacing parts.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit
plain: The computer sees an electrical fault in the circuit for the valve that lets air from the air pump into the exhaust.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the valve resistance and the wiring to it
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit Open
plain: The circuit for the secondary air switching valve appears to be broken, so the valve cannot be switched on.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the valve resistance and the wiring to it
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit Shorted
plain: The circuit for the secondary air switching valve appears to be shorted.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Wiring shorted to ground or power

checks: Check the valve resistance and the wiring to it
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "B" Circuit
plain: The computer sees an electrical fault in the circuit for the second secondary air switching valve.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the valve resistance and the wiring to it
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "B" Circuit Open
plain: The circuit for the second secondary air switching valve appears to be broken.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the valve resistance and the wiring to it
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "B" Circuit Shorted
plain: The circuit for the second secondary air switching valve appears to be shorted.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Wiring shorted to ground or power

checks: Check the valve resistance and the wiring to it
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Relay "A" Circuit
plain: The computer sees a problem in the circuit for the relay that switches the secondary air pump on after a cold start.
symptoms: Air pump does not run, or runs all the time

causes.name: Seized air pump overloading the circuit

checks: Swap the relay with an identical one and retest
Check the fuse and relay socket for corrosion
fix: Often a new relay; if the pump is seized, the pump too.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Relay "B" Circuit
plain: The computer sees a problem in the circuit for the second relay that controls the secondary air injection system.
checks: Swap the relay with a known-good one
Check the fuse and wiring
fix: Usually a new relay or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit
plain: The computer sees an electrical fault with the second EGR temperature sensor, used mostly on diesel engines.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Usually a new sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The second EGR temperature sensor reads values that do not fit how the engine is running.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Usually a new sensor; check the EGR cooler and valve too.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit Low
plain: The second EGR temperature sensor signal is lower than possible.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the shorted wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit High
plain: The second EGR temperature sensor signal is higher than possible, often from an open wire.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The second EGR temperature sensor signal keeps dropping out or jumping around.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the EGR temperature sensor reading against engine temperature when cold
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring near the hot exhaust parts
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace the sensor.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the secondary air switching valve is reading lower voltage than expected, usually from a short to ground or a bad valve.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the valve resistance and the wiring to it
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.
